title: De motu vibratorio laminarum elasticarum, ubi plures novae vibrationum species hactenus non pertractatae evolvuntur

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Euler is finding the normal modes of a vibrating elastic lamina (Euler–Bernoulli beam), governed by -(d²y/dt²) = b⁴ (d⁴y/dx⁴) after scaling. The end x=0 is free and the end x=a is clamped, so this is the cantilever. The separated solution from §XIII is y = cos(θ²t)·(A cos(θx/b) + B sin(θx/b) + C e^{θx/b} + D e^{-θx/b}).

§XIV imposes the four boundary conditions.
(I) Zero bending moment at the free end, y''(0)=0, gives -A + C + D = 0, so A = C + D.
(II) Zero shear force at the free end, y'''(0)=0, gives -B + C - D = 0, so B = C - D.
(III) Zero deflection at the clamped end, y(a)=0, gives A cosΦ + B sinΦ + C e^Φ + D e^{-Φ} = 0.
(IV) Zero slope at the clamped end, y'(a)=0, gives -A sinΦ + B cosΦ + C e^Φ - D e^{-Φ} = 0.

§XV writes Φ = θa/b and substitutes A and B. This leaves two homogeneous linear equations in C and D. Each one yields the ratio C/D:
- C/D = (sinΦ - cosΦ - e^{-Φ}) / (cosΦ + sinΦ + e^Φ)
- C/D = (cosΦ + sinΦ + e^{-Φ}) / (cosΦ - sinΦ + e^Φ)

Setting the two ratios equal (equivalently, a vanishing 2×2 determinant) and cross-multiplying:
- RHS - LHS = (c+s)² + (s-c)² + 2 + 2c(e^Φ + e^{-Φ}).
- This simplifies to 4 + 4c·coshΦ = 0.
- Hence 2 = -cosΦ(e^Φ + e^{-Φ}), i.e. cosΦ·coshΦ = -1.

This is the classical cantilever frequency equation. Its roots are Φ ≈ 1.8751, 4.6941, 7.8548, 10.9955, …, approaching (2k-1)π/2. Once Φ is known, θ = bΦ/a. The next page gives the period of one vibration (Euler's half-cycle convention) as π/θ² ∝ a²/(b²Φ²).
errors: Typographical: equation III has a stray closing parenthesis '...+De^{-θa/b})=0'.
In the closing line the symbol before '= bΦ/a' is blotted in the print; it should read θ = bΦ/a.
No mathematical errors: the four boundary equations, both expressions for C/D, and the resulting equation cosΦ coshΦ = -1 all check out.

ideas.what: Applying free-end (y''=y'''=0) and clamped-end (y=y'=0) conditions to the separated beam solution, giving a 4×4 homogeneous system.
ideas.modern_name: Boundary-value / eigenvalue problem for the clamped-free Euler–Bernoulli beam
ideas.where_published: Euler, Methodus inveniendi (E65, 1744), Additamentum I; earlier Bernoulli–Euler correspondence; E443 recapitulates it

ideas.what: Eliminating the constants to get the frequency equation cosΦ(e^Φ + e^{-Φ}) = -2.
ideas.modern_name: Cantilever characteristic equation cos βL · cosh βL = -1
ideas.where_published: E65 Additamentum I (1744); discussed by Truesdell in Opera omnia II 11.2

deep.surprise_reason: This is a correct, routine rederivation of the well-known cantilever frequency equation, which Euler had already published in 1744. It is well documented by Truesdell. Nothing on the page is new.
transcription_corrections: The final line should read 'quo inuento statim erit θ = bΦ/a'; the θ is blotted in the scan.
The stray ')' in equation III is in the original print, not an OCR error.
